input.question: What is net neutrality?
input.ground_truth: Net neutrality is the concept that every internet service provider *(ISP)* treats every piece of data equally. This means that the ISP doesn't slow packages down when they go to websites that aren't in their favor. This means that ISP A transfers the packages of its own customers just as reliably and just as fast as the packages coming from or going to ISP B. In a nutshell. Internet transfer is equal for everybody

Okay! Imagine the internet is like a big highway, and all the cars on the highway are the websites and videos you want to visit.

Net neutrality is a rule that says all the cars, no matter how big or small, must go at the same speed and nobody can make some cars go slower or block them just because they want to.

So, if you want to watch a cartoon, play a game, or see a picture, the internet treats all of them the same and lets them come to you just as fast. That's what net neutrality means!
